        - article:
          - heading "♧ NOTICE THE PATTERN" [level=3]
          - list:
            - listitem: As the plane moves up, the contour shrinks.
            - listitem: As the plane moves down, the contour expands.
            - listitem: For z=0, contours are x=nπ or y=(n+1/2)π.
            - listitem: For z=±1, the contour collapses to points.
          - button "？ Why do contour curves change this way?"
        - article:
          - heading "⠿ UNDERSTAND THE RULE" [level=3]
          - paragraph: A contour curve (level set) is the set of all (x,y) such that the surface has a constant height z=k.
          - text: Definition
          - paragraph: "For z=f(x,y), the contour curve at level k is {(x,y) in R² | f(x,y)=k}."
          - complementary:
            - text: △ Common Misconception
            - paragraph:
              - text: Thinking the contour is always a circle.
              - text: Not always—shape depends on f(x,y) and k.
        - article:
          - heading "♧ WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Find and sketch the contour for z=sin(x)cos(y) at level k=0.
          - text: "Solution:"
          - paragraph:
            - text: sin(x)cos(y)=0
            - text: ⇒ sin(x)=0 or cos(y)=0
            - text: ⇒ x=nπ or y=(n+1/2)π
          - text: "---- x=nπ | ---- y=(n+1/2)π"
        - article:
          - heading "☆ TRY INDEPENDENTLY" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Find the contour(s) of z=sin(x)cos(y) at level k=0.60.
          - heading "Your Answer" [level=4]

          - button "○ B. sin(x) + cos(y) = 0.60"
          - button "○ C. sin(x) = 0.60 or cos(y) = 0.60"
          - button "○ D. No contour exists for k = 0.60"
        - article:
          - heading "✓ Correct!" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Contours are given by the level set equation f(x,y)=k for the surface z=f(x,y).
